hints: Look closely at where the two C=C bonds are in each molecule, inside the ring and outside the ring.
Full hydrogenation removes all pi bonds, so think what carbon skeleton is left when both double bonds become single.
For bromination, add two Br atoms across each double bond and then count carbons with four different groups to test the chiral centre claim.
walkthrough:
**Compare the two skeletons**

Both molecules are $\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{16}$ isomers. They share the same 1-methylcyclohex-1-ene ring part.

They differ only in the side-chain alkene at C-4: limonene has $-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CH}_2$, terpinolene has $=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2$.

**Test statement 1, excess H2 / Ni**

Hydrogenation adds $\text{H}_2$ across each C=C:
$$\text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{CR}_2 + \text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{CH}-\text{CHR}_2$$
Both the ring alkene and the side-chain alkene become saturated. Both give 1-methyl-4-(propan-2-yl)cyclohexane, often called p-menthane. So statement 1 is correct.

**Test statement 2, hot concentrated KMnO4**

Hot concentrated acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ cleaves C=C bonds completely. The ring C=C cleaves the same way in both, opening the ring.

The side chain cleaves differently: $\text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}_2$ gives a ketone + $\text{CO}_2$, while $\text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{CMe}_2$ gives a ketone + propanone. The combination of ring opening plus side-chain oxidation gives a diketo acid in each case, but with a different carbon skeleton. So statement 2 is correct.

**Test statement 3, excess Br2 and chirality**

Excess $\text{Br}_2$ adds across both double bonds to give tetrabromides of formula $\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{16}\text{Br}_4$:
$$\text{C}=\text{C} + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{CBr}-\text{CBr}$$
Because Br adds in different positions on the side chain, the two products are positional isomers. That part is true.

Now count chiral carbons, a carbon with four different groups. Limonene tetrabromide has 4 chiral centres: the two ring C-Br carbons, the ring C-4, and the side-chain $\text{CBr}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ carbon. Terpinolene tetrabromide has only 3 chiral centres: the two ring C-Br carbons and the ring C-4, because the side-chain $\text{CBr}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ carbon has two identical methyl groups and is achiral. So the same number claim is false, making statement 3 false.

**Conclude**

Statements 1 and 2 are correct, statement 3 is incorrect. That matches 1, 2 only.

options.A: This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 1 and 2 are correct, but 3 fails because although the tetrabromides are positional isomers, they do not have the same number of chiral carbons, limonene product has 4 and terpinolene product has 3.
options.B: This option claims 1 and 2 only are correct. Hydrogenation gives the same p-menthane in both cases, and vigorous oxidative cleavage gives different diketo acids because the side-chain alkenes cleave to different fragments. Statement 3 is false on chirality count.
options.C: This option claims 2 and 3 only are correct. Statement 2 is correct, but it wrongly includes 3 and wrongly excludes 1. Statement 1 is definitely correct, and statement 3 is incorrect due to different numbers of chiral centres.
options.D: This option claims 1 only is correct. Statement 1 is correct, but statement 2 is also correct. Hot concentrated KMnO4 cleavage of the different side-chain alkenes gives different diketo acids, so 2 should also be included.
